Package io.github.jabrena.juno.jdk.net.http

@NullMarked package io.github.jabrena.juno.jdk.net.http
Board-side implementations of java.net.http: the JDK's HTTP client syntax on the board. The compiler reads every class here under java.net.http, so a program written against the JDK's HttpClient, HttpRequest, HttpResponse and HttpHeaders runs this code, which sends the request through NativeHttpRequests.

It runs on the UNO R4 WiFi and larger boards; the compiler rejects it on the UNO R3. It is a subset, shaped by the board's fixed memory:

  • URIs: any http or https URI with a host, of any length;
  • a client is AutoCloseable, as in the JDK since 21: close, shutdown and shutdownNow stop it from sending, and isTerminated and awaitTermination answer at once, since every request runs to completion in the thread that sends it;
  • synchronous send only, over HTTP/1.1 whatever version asks for; no sendAsync, cookies or authenticator;
  • requests: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD and method(...) for any other method. Unlike the JDK, CONNECT is sent too, to the URI's host:port, and reports its status, but opens no usable tunnel: the board closes the connection after the response; headers with header, headers and setHeader, at most 512 bytes of them; bodies from BodyPublishers.ofString (at most 512 bytes), ofByteArray and noBody. A body without a Content-Type header is sent as application/json, the board's default, where the JDK sends none;
  • responses: BodyHandlers.ofByteArray() and BodyHandlers.ofString(). With ofByteArray() the client receives the body into a buffer of fixed capacity, 384 bytes, refilled by each request and zero-filled past the bytes received, so a longer body is truncated and body().length is the capacity rather than the size received; that path allocates nothing per request. With ofString() the body is a String of every byte received, not decoded, sized to the response (Content-Length, or grown as a chunked body arrives), with no limit but the free memory: a body that does not fit fails the request with an IOException;
  • headers(): firstValue and firstValueAsLong, from a buffer of 512 bytes that each request refills; a program that never reads headers or follows redirects keeps a 16-byte buffer instead;
  • redirects: followRedirects(NEVER | ALWAYS | NORMAL), at most 5 per request, to an absolute URI or an absolute path; only to a scheme one of the program's own URIs names, since only those requests are linked;
  • timeouts: HttpRequest.Builder.timeout and HttpClient.Builder.connectTimeout. The board has one timeout for the whole exchange, the request's if it has one, else the client's, else 5000 ms; no response within it throws HttpTimeoutException;
  • the client allocates its buffers once, when it is built. With ofByteArray() and no redirect, send allocates nothing, as the response is the client's own; with ofString() each response allocates its String, and each redirect followed allocates the next URI;
  • a request that fails throws IOException, as the JDK does.
